downforceLow.why: Slow-corner downforce: the front wing sets turn-in, the floor carries the load, and ride control from the suspension matters at low speed. Starting weights; M2 calibrates.

downforceHigh.why: High-speed downforce in the ground-effect era comes mostly from the floor; the sidepods feed it clean air.

drag.why: Drag efficiency of the parts; the car's drag rating is 100 minus this, so better parts mean less drag for the same downforce.

dirtyAirTolerance.why: How much of its grip the car keeps in the wake of another: underfloor downforce is robust, a wing-dependent front end is not.

mechanicalGrip.why: Grip that does not depend on speed: mostly suspension kinematics, some from how stable the platform keeps the floor.

brakingStability.why: Stability on the brakes: the brake system itself plus how the suspension controls pitch.

rideHeightSensitivity.why: Porpoising resistance of the parts; the car's sensitivity rating is 100 minus this.

tyreManagement.why: How gently the car treats its tyres: suspension compliance first, then aero platform stability, brake and cooling temperatures.

chassisReliability.why: Chassis side of reliability: gearbox failures, cooling (sidepods) and brakes are the usual non-engine retirements.

overweightKgAtRating0.why: Kilograms above the minimum weight for a car whose parts all rate 0; falls linearly to 0 kg at rating 100. Real cars were 5–15 kg over in 2022.

powerUnitShareOfReliability.why: The power unit causes most mechanical retirements, so it carries 60% of overall reliability; the chassis the rest.
